topic: Pilates for tennis and pickleball players

slides.headline: More court time, fewer niggles
slides.sub: What clinical Pilates adds for tennis and pickleball players.

slides.title: Quick feet need strong hips
slides.body: Side shuffles and sudden stops load the hips, knees and ankles. Single-leg work on the reformer builds control, so each lunge towards the ball can feel steadier.

slides.title: Rotation comes from the trunk
slides.body: Groundstrokes and dinks rely on turning through the mid-back and hips. Pilates exercises that train controlled rotation can help share load away from the shoulder and elbow.

slides.title: Shoulders that handle the serve
slides.body: Serves and smashes ask a lot of the rotator cuff and shoulder blade muscles. Spring-loaded arm work builds strength through range, with resistance that's easy to adjust.

slides.title: Balance for the split step
slides.body: Being ready on your toes takes calf strength and balance. Standing and reformer balance work can help you react quicker and land more comfortably between shots.

slides.title: Fits around your game days
slides.body: Most players do well with one or two sessions a week, placed away from big match days. Your program can be adjusted when you're playing more or nursing a niggle.

slides.headline: Want a program for the court?
slides.body: Our Pilates team starts with an assessment, then builds exercises around your sport and your schedule. Book online, link in bio.

caption:
Hooked on tennis or pickleball? Here's what clinical Pilates can add to your game. 🎾

Both sports ask for quick side-to-side footwork, controlled rotation and shoulders that can handle repeated overhead shots. Pilates trains those qualities with spring resistance that's easy to adjust: single-leg control for your lunges, trunk rotation for your groundstrokes, and shoulder strength through range for your serve.

Most players find one or two sessions a week fits nicely around game days, and the program can shift when you're playing more or managing a niggle.

story.headline: Tennis or pickleball regular?
story.body: Add single-leg balance work twice a week. Steadier legs make every lunge towards the ball feel easier.
